10.1002_smll.202511617: The development of luminol‐based cathodic electrochemiluminescence (ECL) systems has been hindered by the inherent difficulties of direct electro‐oxidation of luminol at negative potentials and low conversion efficiency of coreactants to reactive oxygen species (ROS). Additionally, the deprotonation of luminol intermediates requires strongly alkaline condition, restricting its application in bioanalysis. In this work, a facile one‐step synthesized 2D conductive copper tetrahydroxyquinone (Cu‐THQ) metal‐organic framework is introduced as a coreaction accelerator into the luminol/H 2 O 2 system, achieving a super‐enhanced efficiency of luminol cathodic ECL in neutral solution, the ECL signal is amplified by nearly 4500 times with excellent stability. Comprehensive characterizations using electrochemical methods, multiple spectroscopic techniques, and in situ pH monitoring revealed that Cu‐O 4 active sites in Cu‐THQ exhibit a dual‐catalytic mechanism for H 2 O 2 and H 2 O, that is, catalyzing H 2 O 2 to generate abundant ROS and electrolyzing water to provide a localized alkaline microenvironment, thus facilitating ECL of luminol. Theoretical calculation further demonstrated the strong adsorption and catalytic performance of the Cu‐O 4 active center toward H 2 O 2 . Utilizing the strong and stable cathodic ECL of luminol/H 2 O 2 /Cu‐THQ ternary system, a label‐free immunosensor is constructed for ultrasensitive detection of p‐Tau181, an important biomarker for Alzheimer's disease, achieving a detection limit of 4.56 fg mL −1 .
10.1002_smll.202514809: Persistent interfacial defects and instability remain key limitations for high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs), motivating the development of multifunctional materials that can simultaneously enable efficient charge transport and defect passivation. Here, we report a molecularly engineered dibenzo[g,p]chrysene (DBC)‐based core molecule winged by N‐(4‐methoxyphenyl)pyren‐1‐amine units, SP‐07, designed to operate in two distinct yet complementary roles: as a dopant‐free hole‐transport material (HTM) and as an interfacial passivation layer. Owing to its planar conjugated core and electron‐rich functional groups, SP‐07 exhibits high intrinsic hole mobility (∼28.7 × 10 −4 cm 2 /V·s), uniform film formation, and efficient charge extraction. When employed as a standalone HTM, SP‐07‐based PSCs achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.7% and demonstrate exceptional operational stability under continuous illumination at 85°C, outperforming spiro‐OMeTAD‐based reference devices. On the other hand, acting as a passivation layer, SP‐07 constructively mitigates under‐coordinated Pb 2+ /halide defects, reduces trap‐assisted recombination, improves surface hydrophobicity, and maintains perovskite crystallinity, resulting in devices with a champion PCE exceeding 23%. Outstandingly, passivated devices retain ∼95% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous operation under thermal and illumination stress and maintain structural integrity under ambient conditions for 30 days. These findings demonstrate that the dual functionality of SP‐07 enables synergistic improvements in both efficiency and long‐term stability, providing a promising strategy for advancing PSCs.
